title: OmniVia Core Application Contract v1 - errors
description: Stable error semantics. `ErrorCode` and `RetryClass` are deliberately open patterned strings rather than closed JSON Schema enums, so a compatible minor release can add vocabulary without breaking existing decoders. The frozen v1 vocabulary is carried as annotations below and is the source the code generator reads.

x-omnivia-retry-classes.non_retryable: Retrying the identical request cannot succeed. Surface the failure.
x-omnivia-retry-classes.retryable: The identical request may succeed if retried; no minimum delay is implied.
x-omnivia-retry-classes.retryable_after_delay: Retry only after backing off. Honour `retry_after_ms` when present.
x-omnivia-retry-classes.retryable_after_precondition_refresh: The request is only safe to retry after re-reading the record and rebuilding `mutation_precondition`. Never blind-retry.

ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode
ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable failure code. OPEN by design: this is a patterned string, not an enum, so compatible minor releases can add codes. Decoders must preserve unknown codes and must not map them onto a known code.

RetryClass.title: RetryClass
RetryClass.description: How a caller may retry. OPEN by design, for the same reason as `ErrorCode`. An unrecognized retry class MUST fail safe as non-retryable: never infer that an unknown class is retryable.

ApiError.title: ApiError
ApiError.description: A single typed failure. The code and retry class are the contract; the message is not.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Never parse it and never branch on it.

retry_class.description: Retry semantics for this failure. Unknown values are treated as non-retryable.

retry_after_ms.description: Minimum backoff before a retry is worth attempting, when the server can state one.

details.description: Optional structured detail. Must never carry credentials.
